method_card.title: Bar Charts, Pie Charts and Stem-and-Leaf Diagrams
method_card.content:
A pie chart represents data as sectors of a circle. The formula for each sector angle is given on the formula sheet: \(\text{angle} = \frac{\text{frequency}}{\text{total}} \times 360\). Always divide by the total frequency, not by the number of categories.

A comparative pie chart uses two circles of different sizes to compare two datasets. The areas of the circles are proportional to the totals, so a dataset with twice the total has a circle with \(\sqrt{2}\) times the radius — not twice the radius. This is a Higher-tier skill.

For a stem-and-leaf diagram, the stem is the leading digit(s) and the leaf is the final digit. Always include a key (e.g. 3 | 7 means 37). A back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram places two datasets either side of a shared stem; left-side leaves are read from right to left (they increase outward from the stem).

Bar charts come in several forms: a dual bar chart places two bars side by side. A composite (stacked) bar chart stacks bars to show both the total and components. A percentage bar chart standardises all bars to 100%.

When reading a Venn diagram, the intersection represents items in both categories. P(A only) excludes the intersection; always check whether the question asks for a count or a probability.
steps: For a pie sector angle, divide the category frequency by the total, then multiply by 360
For a stem-and-leaf diagram, split each value into its stem (leading digit) and leaf (final digit)
Write the key for any stem-and-leaf diagram (e.g. 2 | 4 means 24)
For back-to-back diagrams, read left-side leaves from right to left
For a Venn diagram, identify the intersection, left-only, right-only and outside regions before answering
For comparative pie charts (Higher), check whether you are comparing angles or actual frequencies

exam_context.marks: 2–5 marks; sector angle calculations are 2 marks, back-to-back stem-and-leaf comparisons up to 4 marks
exam_context.frequency: Pie chart sector angles and stem-and-leaf reading appear on most papers; Venn diagram intersection questions appear on roughly half of all papers

worked_examples.question: 30 students were asked their favourite subject. 12 chose Maths. What angle is needed for the Maths sector in a pie chart?

A back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram shows test scores. Class A (left): stem 5 leaves 9,8,3; stem 6 leaves 7,2; stem 7 leaves 5,1. Class B (right): stem 5 leaves 1,4; stem 6 leaves 0,6,8; stem 7 leaves 3,7,9. Key: 6|2 means 62. Find the median for each class.

steps.label: Step 1 — List Class A in order
Step 2 — List Class B in order
steps.content: 51, 54, 60, 66, 68, 73, 77, 79 — 8 values, median is average of 4th and 5th: \(\frac{66+68}{2} = 67\)

worked_examples.question: A Venn diagram shows 40 students. 24 study History, 18 study Geography, and 8 study both. How many study neither? What is the probability a randomly chosen student studies History only?

steps.label: Step 1 — Find History only and Geography only
Step 2 — Find those in at least one subject
Step 3 — Find neither and the probability

bronze.display: A survey of 60 people found 15 preferred tea. What angle represents the tea sector in a pie chart?

misconceptions.message: Angle = (15/60) × 360 = 0.25 × 360 = 90°. Divide by the total (60).

bronze.display: A pie chart sector for 'Cycling' has an angle of 72°. The pie chart represents 100 people. How many chose cycling?

misconceptions.message: Frequency = (72/360) × 100 = 0.2 × 100 = 20. Reverse the sector-angle formula.

bronze.display: A stem-and-leaf diagram has key: 4 | 7 means 47. The stem 3 row has leaves 2, 5, 8, 8. What is the largest value in the stem 3 row?

misconceptions.message: Stem 3 with leaf 8 means 38. Each leaf is a single digit appended to the stem.

bronze.display: A dual bar chart shows sales for two shops. Shop A January: 40 units; Shop B January: 55 units. How many more units did Shop B sell in January?

misconceptions.message: 55 − 40 = 15 units. Read each bar from zero.

bronze.display: A pie chart has four sectors with angles 90°, 120°, 80°, and x°. Find x.

misconceptions.message: All sector angles sum to 360°. x = 360 − (90 + 120 + 80) = 70°.

bronze.display: Which property can be directly compared from a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram?
options: The range and median of both datasets simultaneously
The mean of both datasets without any calculation
The exact variance of each dataset
The cumulative frequency of each dataset

misconceptions.message: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf shows the shape, spread (range) and median visually for both sets at once. The mean requires calculation.

bronze.display: 48 students were surveyed. 20 play a team sport, 15 do an individual sport, and 7 do both. How many students do neither?

misconceptions.message: Team only: 20 − 7 = 13. Individual only: 15 − 7 = 8. In at least one: 13 + 8 + 7 = 28. Neither: 48 − 28 = 20.

bronze.display: A pie chart is drawn for: Red: 18, Blue: 12, Green: 6, Yellow: 4. What is the total frequency needed before calculating any sector angle?

misconceptions.message: Total = 18 + 12 + 6 + 4 = 40. You must find the total before calculating any sector angle.

silver.display: A survey of 45 students found: 18 prefer football, 12 prefer tennis, 9 prefer swimming, 6 prefer other. Calculate the sector angle for the swimming category.

misconceptions.message: Angle = (9/45) × 360 = 0.2 × 360 = 72°. Divide by total 45.

silver.display: A stem-and-leaf diagram for 9 values (key 2|3 means 23) shows stems 1, 2, 3 with leaves: 1|5,8; 2|0,3,7; 3|1,4,9. Find the median.

misconceptions.message: 9 values ordered: 15, 18, 20, 23, 27, 31, 34, 39. Wait — check: 9 values means median is 5th. Values: 15,18,20,23,27,31,34,39 — that is 8 listed. Re-count leaves: 1|5,8 (2); 2|0,3,7 (3); 3|1,4,9 (3). Total = 8 values, median = average of 4th and 5th = (23+27)/2 = 25. For odd n=9: if there are 9 leaves the median is the 5th.

silver.display: A composite bar chart shows two products. Product A: 30 online, 20 in-store (total 50). Product B: 45 online, 15 in-store (total 60). What percentage of Product B's sales were in-store?

misconceptions.message: In-store for B = 15, total for B = 60. Percentage = (15/60) × 100 = 25%. Do not use Product A's total.

silver.display: In a Venn diagram of 50 students, 30 own a dog and 22 own a cat. 8 own both. What is the probability that a randomly chosen student owns a cat but not a dog?

misconceptions.message: Cat only = 22 − 8 = 14. P(cat only) = 14/50 = 7/25. The denominator is the total 50.

silver.display: A percentage bar chart shows Year 10: 40% grade 4+ (120 students) and Year 11: 65% grade 4+ (80 students). How many more Year 11 students than Year 10 students achieved grade 4+?

misconceptions.message: Year 10: 40% of 120 = 48. Year 11: 65% of 80 = 52. Year 11 has 52 − 48 = 4 more. Don't compare percentages when group sizes differ.

silver.display: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf shows run times. Runner A (left from stem): 2|3,7,9; 3|1,5; 4|0. Runner B (right from stem): 2|1,5; 3|0,2,8; 4|4,6. Key: 3|1 means 31 minutes. Which runner has the smaller range?

misconceptions.message: Runner A: min = 23, max = 40, range = 17. Runner B: min = 21, max = 46, range = 25. Always order leaves to find the minimum and maximum.

gold.display: A survey of 80 people asked about two streaming services. 52 use Service A, 45 use Service B, 28 use both. How many use neither service?
A pie chart represents 120 people. The sector for 'Bus' has angle 75°. How many people chose Bus?
A back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram shows 9 values for Dataset X. X (left): stem 4|8,5,2; stem 5|9,3,1; stem 6|7,4,0. Find the interquartile range of Dataset X.

misconceptions.message: X ordered: 42,45,48,51,53,59,60,64,67. n=9 (one less than 12, a multiple of 4). Q1 = 2nd+3rd avg? No — for n=9 in AQA spec, Q1 = (9+1)/4 = 2.5th position = (45+48)/2 = 46.5; Q3 = 7.5th = (60+64)/2 = 62. IQR = 62−46.5 = 15.5. Check leaves read right-to-left from stem.
Left-side leaves in a back-to-back diagram are read from right to left (outward from the stem). The values for X are 42,45,48 (stem 4), 51,53,59 (stem 5), 60,64,67 (stem 6).

gold.display: A composite bar chart: Group 1 total bar = 80, with segment A = 30, segment B = 25. What percentage of Group 1's bar is segment C?
A three-circle Venn diagram has total 100. M only: 20; N only: 15; P only: 25; M∩N only: 8; M∩P only: 6; N∩P only: 4; M∩N∩P: 3. How many outcomes are in none of the three events?

misconceptions.message: In a three-circle Venn diagram, pairwise intersections do NOT include the triple intersection — the values given are for each distinct region.
